report_metadata.sdlc_rationale: Requirements fully defined and signed off by CFO; team has direct experience with mandated stack (React, Java, PostgreSQL, AWS, Okta); fixed deadline with no flexibility; changes mid-project not expected.

project_understanding.primary_goal: Replace legacy internal expense report tool with a greenfield web app enabling employees to submit receipts and approvals online, with nightly export to SAP ERP.
project_understanding.beneficiary: 400 employees (submitters) and finance team (approvers/exporters); CFO and IT Director (governance).
project_understanding.trigger: Legacy tool is no longer maintainable; fiscal calendar alignment creates hard deadline; volume (3k submissions/month) requires scalable solution.
success_definition: ≥95% of submissions require zero finance rework (data quality metric)
Median approval cycle under 48 hours (process efficiency)
User satisfaction survey ≥4.2/5 after 90 days (adoption metric)
supporting_quotes: Replace our legacy internal expense report tool with a greenfield web app
Employees submit receipts and approvals online; finance exports to the existing ERP (SAP) nightly
≥95% of submissions need zero finance rework; median approval cycle under 48h; user satisfaction survey ≥ 4.2/5 after 90 days

assumption_log.what: The 0.5 QA allocation (shared pool) is confirmed available full-time equivalent across the project duration (24 weeks), not fractional per-week.
assumption_log.why: Input specifies '0.5 QA (shared)' without clarifying whether this is a dedicated 50% FTE or a shared resource pulled on-demand. For a project with hard deadline and SOC 2 compliance, QA must be reliably available. Assuming dedicated 50% FTE allows planning; if actual availability is lower, critical path slips.
assumption_log.pmi_basis: PMBOK 6th Ed, Section 9.2 — Resource availability must be confirmed before schedule baseline is set.
assumption_log.consequence: If QA is actually on-demand (not dedicated), Phase 4 testing will extend 2-3 weeks, pushing past 2026-09-01 deadline. SOC 2 audit readiness will be at risk.
assumption_log.tradeoff: Gains: allows schedule to be defensible with stated team. Risks: if QA is truly fractional and pulled to other projects, timeline becomes unachievable.

assumption_log.what: The 0.5 PM allocation is sufficient to manage scope, stakeholder alignment, and delivery across all 5 phases without additional PM support.
assumption_log.why: Input specifies PM at 0.5 (50% FTE). For a 24-week project with 3 named stakeholders (CFO, IT Director, Internal Audit), 0.5 PM is lean but feasible if the PM is experienced and scope is locked. Assuming this is a dedicated 50% FTE, not ad-hoc.
assumption_log.pmi_basis: PMBOK 6th Ed, Section 9.2 — PM allocation must be proportionate to stakeholder complexity and scope risk.
assumption_log.consequence: If PM is pulled to other initiatives or stakeholder alignment requires more than 50% effort, scope creep and stakeholder misalignment will occur. Deadline will slip.
assumption_log.tradeoff: Gains: allows plan to proceed with stated team size. Risks: if PM is fractional and competing priorities emerge, governance and change control will suffer.

assumption_log.what: SAP API integration is stable, documented, and sandbox access is already confirmed by IT Director. No additional discovery or vendor coordination is required in Phase 1.
assumption_log.why: Input states 'finance exports to the existing ERP (SAP) nightly' and lists IT Director as stakeholder/sign-off. This implies SAP integration is a known, existing capability. Assuming IT has already validated API availability and schema; no discovery delay expected.
assumption_log.pmi_basis: PMBOK 6th Ed, Section 11.2 — Integration risks must be identified early; if SAP API is unknown or undocumented, Phase 1 discovery extends.
assumption_log.consequence: If SAP API is undocumented, rate-limited, or requires custom development, Phase 2-3 will extend 2-4 weeks. Budget may exceed $120k.
assumption_log.tradeoff: Gains: allows Phase 1 to focus on requirements and UX design, not API discovery. Risks: if SAP integration is more complex than assumed, critical path extends.

assumption_log.what: Okta SSO integration is a standard, pre-configured service within the AWS org account. No custom authentication development is required.
assumption_log.why: Input specifies 'SSO via Okta' as a mandated stack element. Okta is a standard identity provider; assuming IT has already provisioned Okta in the AWS account and provided integration documentation. No custom auth code needed.
assumption_log.pmi_basis: PMBOK 6th Ed, Section 5.4 — Scope baseline assumes standard, pre-existing infrastructure.
assumption_log.consequence: If Okta is not yet provisioned or requires custom configuration, Phase 2 development will be delayed 1-2 weeks.
assumption_log.tradeoff: Gains: allows frontend and backend to use standard Okta libraries without custom work. Risks: if Okta is not ready, authentication becomes a blocker.

critical_path_summary.staffing_implication: Backend Developer and Frontend Developer must be allocated full-time (100%) across Phases 2-4; PM must be protected from competing projects to maintain stakeholder alignment and change control.

phases.name: Discovery & Design
milestones: Requirements document finalized and signed by CFO
SOC 2 control requirements mapped to design

tasks.name: Conduct stakeholder alignment session and document scope sign-off
tasks.definition_of_done: Scope document signed by CFO, IT Director, and Internal Audit; no open questions on must-haves vs. out-of-scope.

tasks.name: Conduct user research with 5-10 employee submitters and 3 finance approvers
tasks.definition_of_done: User personas documented; pain points and workflow mapped; findings shared with team.

tasks.name: Write detailed API specifications for receipt capture, policy rules engine, and approval chain
tasks.definition_of_done: API spec document reviewed and approved by IT Director; all endpoints, request/response schemas, and error codes defined.

tasks.name: Validate SAP API rate limits and batch window strategy with IT
tasks.definition_of_done: SAP API documentation reviewed; batch window schedule confirmed; rate limit handling strategy documented.

tasks.name: Design database schema for expense reports, receipts, approvals, and audit logs
tasks.definition_of_done: Schema diagram and DDL scripts reviewed by IT Director; SOC 2 audit trail requirements mapped to schema.

tasks.name: Create UX wireframes for receipt capture, approval workflow, and error dashboard
tasks.definition_of_done: Wireframes approved by CFO and at least one employee submitter; accessibility checklist (WCAG 2.1 AA) completed.

phases.name: Core Development
milestones: Receipt capture (camera + PDF upload) working end-to-end
Policy rules engine evaluating expense policies
SAP export job running in sandbox

tasks.name: Implement receipt capture UI (camera + PDF upload) in React
tasks.definition_of_done: Receipt upload working in dev environment; file validation (size, format) implemented; error messages user-friendly.

tasks.name: Implement policy rules engine (Java Spring Boot) for expense validation
tasks.definition_of_done: Rules engine evaluates all must-have policies (amount limits, category rules); test coverage ≥80%; rules can be updated without code deployment.

tasks.name: Implement manager approval workflow UI in React
tasks.definition_of_done: Approval chain UI displays pending reports; managers can approve/reject with comments; notifications sent via email.

tasks.name: Implement approval chain backend logic and notifications
tasks.definition_of_done: Approval state machine working; email notifications sent; audit log records all approval actions.

tasks.name: Implement Okta SSO integration for authentication
tasks.definition_of_done: Users can log in via Okta; session management working; logout clears session.

tasks.name: Implement SAP export job (nightly batch) in Java
tasks.definition_of_done: Export job runs nightly in sandbox; approved reports sent to SAP; error handling logs failures to error dashboard.

tasks.name: Implement error dashboard for finance team
tasks.definition_of_done: Dashboard displays failed exports, error messages, and retry options; finance can filter by date and status.

tasks.name: Internal demo preparation and stakeholder walkthrough
tasks.definition_of_done: Demo script prepared; stakeholders see working receipt capture, approval chain, and SAP export; feedback documented.

phases.name: Integration & Edge Cases
milestones: All integrations tested end-to-end (Okta, SAP, email)
Edge case handling implemented (OCR errors, rate limits, duplicate submissions)
Security review completed by IT Director

tasks.name: Implement OCR error handling and human review queue
tasks.definition_of_done: OCR confidence scores calculated; low-confidence receipts routed to finance review queue; queue UI shows pending items.

tasks.name: Implement duplicate submission detection and handling
tasks.definition_of_done: System detects duplicate receipts (same amount, date, vendor within 24h); user warned before submission; audit log records detection.

tasks.name: Test SAP API rate limiting and batch window handling
tasks.definition_of_done: Export job tested with 3k submissions/month volume; rate limit handling verified; batch window respected; no data loss on retry.

tasks.name: Conduct security review and implement SOC 2 controls
tasks.definition_of_done: Security review completed by IT Director; all SOC 2 control requirements implemented (encryption at rest, audit logging, access controls); no PAN data stored.

tasks.name: Implement audit logging for all user actions and system events
tasks.definition_of_done: All user actions (submit, approve, reject) logged with timestamp, user ID, and action details; Internal Audit can query logs.

tasks.name: End-to-end integration testing (Okta, SAP, email, audit logs)
tasks.definition_of_done: Full workflow tested: user logs in via Okta, submits receipt, manager approves, report exported to SAP, audit log recorded; no data loss.

phases.name: QA & Testing
milestones: UAT completed with employee submitters and finance team

tasks.name: Execute comprehensive test plan (functional, regression, performance)
tasks.definition_of_done: Test plan executed; all critical and high bugs fixed; medium/low bugs documented for post-launch; test coverage ≥85%.

tasks.name: Conduct UAT with 10 employee submitters and 3 finance approvers
tasks.definition_of_done: UAT completed; feedback collected; user satisfaction baseline established; sign-off from CFO on readiness.

tasks.name: Performance testing at 3k submissions/month volume
tasks.definition_of_done: Load test simulates 3k submissions/month; response times < 2s; database queries optimized; no timeouts.

tasks.name: Accessibility audit (WCAG 2.1 AA compliance)
tasks.definition_of_done: Automated accessibility scan passed; manual review completed; keyboard navigation working; screen reader compatible.

tasks.name: Prepare runbooks and operational handoff documentation
tasks.definition_of_done: Runbooks document deployment, monitoring, alerting, and incident response; IT Director reviewed and approved.

tasks.name: Prepare user training materials and adoption plan
tasks.definition_of_done: Training videos, user guide, and FAQ prepared; adoption plan includes email campaign and manager briefings.

tasks.name: Deploy to production and execute smoke tests
tasks.definition_of_done: Application deployed to production; smoke tests passed; no critical errors in logs; rollback plan tested.

tasks.name: Launch user training and adoption campaign
tasks.definition_of_done: Training emails sent; manager briefings completed; help desk briefed; adoption metrics baseline established.

tasks.name: Handoff to IT operations and establish post-launch support
tasks.definition_of_done: IT operations team trained on monitoring and incident response; on-call rotation established; escalation path documented.

risk_register.description: If QA allocation (0.5 FTE shared pool) is pulled to competing projects, Phase 4 testing will extend 2-3 weeks, pushing past 2026-09-01 deadline and delaying SOC 2 audit readiness.
risk_register.trigger: QA resource is reassigned mid-project or becomes unavailable for more than 1 week.
risk_register.mitigation: Secure written commitment from QA pool manager that 0.5 FTE is reserved and protected for this project through Phase 4. Establish weekly check-ins to confirm availability.
risk_register.contingency: If QA becomes unavailable, hire contract QA engineer immediately (budget allows ~$15k for 4-week contract). Compress Phase 4 by deferring non-critical bug fixes to post-launch.

risk_register.description: If SAP API rate limits are more restrictive than assumed or batch window is shorter than expected, nightly export job will fail to complete within the window, causing data backlog and finance rework.
risk_register.trigger: SAP API documentation reveals rate limits lower than 3k submissions/month or batch window is < 4 hours.
risk_register.mitigation: Validate SAP API rate limits and batch window in Phase 1 (T4). Implement export job with exponential backoff and queue persistence in Phase 2 (T12). Test at production volume in Phase 3 (T17).
risk_register.contingency: If rate limits are exceeded, implement multi-batch strategy (split exports across multiple windows) or negotiate higher rate limits with SAP team. Worst case: defer non-critical exports to next batch window.

risk_register.description: If OCR accuracy is lower than expected (< 85% confidence), human review queue will become a bottleneck, delaying approvals and missing the 48-hour median approval cycle target.
risk_register.trigger: OCR confidence scores are < 85% for > 20% of receipts during Phase 3 testing.
risk_register.mitigation: Implement OCR confidence scoring in Phase 3 (T15). Route low-confidence receipts to finance review queue. Set confidence threshold based on Phase 3 testing results.
risk_register.contingency: If OCR accuracy is too low, increase manual review capacity (finance team) or implement secondary OCR provider (e.g., Google Vision API) for low-confidence items.

risk_register.description: If stakeholders request scope additions (e.g., international per-diem rules, corporate card integration) during development, timeline will slip and budget will be exceeded.
risk_register.trigger: Stakeholder requests features not in the signed scope document or CFO asks for 'quick additions' during Phase 2-3.
risk_register.mitigation: Establish formal change control process in Phase 1. Document out-of-scope items (international per-diem, corporate card) as Phase 2 work. Require CFO sign-off on any scope changes.
risk_register.contingency: If scope creep occurs, defer new features to Phase 2 and adjust timeline/budget accordingly. Do not add to critical path.

risk_register.description: If SOC 2 audit requirements are more extensive than assumed (e.g., additional encryption, access controls, or compliance certifications), Phase 3 security review will extend and delay go-live.
risk_register.trigger: IT Director or Internal Audit identifies additional SOC 2 controls during Phase 3 security review.
risk_register.mitigation: Map all SOC 2 control requirements to design in Phase 1 (T5). Conduct pre-review with IT Director before Phase 3 security review (T18). Implement controls incrementally during Phase 2-3.
risk_register.contingency: If additional controls are required, prioritize critical controls for go-live and defer non-critical controls to post-launch (with documented risk acceptance from CFO).

risk_register.description: If Phase 1 requirements discovery is incomplete or stakeholder alignment is not achieved, Phase 2 development will be blocked or rework will be required, pushing timeline past 2026-09-01.
risk_register.trigger: Stakeholders disagree on scope, success criteria, or approval workflow during Phase 1.
risk_register.mitigation: Conduct formal stakeholder alignment session in Phase 1 (T1). Document scope and success criteria in writing. Require CFO, IT Director, and Internal Audit sign-off before Phase 2 starts.
risk_register.contingency: If alignment is not achieved, extend Phase 1 by 1 week and conduct additional stakeholder workshops. Do not start Phase 2 until scope is locked.

risk_register.description: If the 0.5 PM allocation is insufficient to manage 3 stakeholders (CFO, IT Director, Internal Audit) and scope changes, stakeholder misalignment and scope creep will occur.
risk_register.trigger: PM reports spending > 50% time on stakeholder management or stakeholders express dissatisfaction with communication.
risk_register.mitigation: Establish weekly stakeholder sync meetings (30 min each) in Phase 1. Delegate scope change decisions to CFO. Create shared project dashboard for transparency.
risk_register.contingency: If PM is overloaded, hire contract PM for 0.25 FTE to handle stakeholder communication and change control. Budget allows ~$10k for 8-week contract.

risk_register.description: If the frontend developer lacks experience with React 18 or TypeScript, Phase 2 development will be slower and code quality will suffer, extending timeline.
risk_register.trigger: Frontend developer struggles with React 18 patterns or TypeScript type system during Phase 2.
risk_register.mitigation: Confirm frontend developer has React 18 and TypeScript experience before Phase 2 starts. Allocate 2-3 days for ramp-up on project-specific patterns.
risk_register.contingency: If developer lacks experience, pair with backend developer for code reviews and provide TypeScript training. Consider hiring contract React specialist for 2-3 weeks.

risk_register.description: If Okta SSO integration is not pre-configured in the AWS account, Phase 2 authentication development will be blocked or delayed.
risk_register.trigger: IT Director confirms Okta is not yet provisioned or requires custom configuration.
risk_register.mitigation: Validate Okta provisioning in Phase 1 (T4). Request IT to provision Okta before Phase 2 starts. Have fallback local authentication ready if Okta is delayed.
risk_register.contingency: If Okta is not ready, implement local authentication in Phase 2 and integrate Okta in Phase 3. This adds 1-2 weeks to Phase 3.

staffing_plan.notes: 0.5 FTE across all phases. Must be protected from competing projects. Responsible for stakeholder alignment, scope control, and go-live readiness. Weekly stakeholder syncs required.
Full-time (100% allocation) across all phases. Critical path owner for API design, policy rules engine, SAP export job, and security controls. Must have experience with Spring Boot and PostgreSQL.
Full-time (100% allocation) across Phases 2-4. Responsible for receipt capture UI, approval workflow UI, and error dashboard. Must have React 18 and TypeScript experience.

0.5 FTE (shared pool) across Phases 3-4. Must be protected from competing projects. Responsible for comprehensive testing, UAT coordination, and performance validation. Minimum 25% of dev hours (320h × 25% = 80h) — this allocation meets the requirement.
0.5 FTE front-loaded (Phases 1-2). Responsible for user research, wireframes, and accessibility audit. Can be shared with other projects after Phase 2.

open_questions.question: Is the 0.5 QA allocation a dedicated, protected FTE for this project, or is QA available on-demand from a shared pool that may be pulled to other priorities?
open_questions.impact_if_unanswered: If QA is on-demand and not protected, Phase 4 testing will extend 2-3 weeks, pushing past the 2026-09-01 deadline. SOC 2 audit readiness will be at risk.

open_questions.question: Has IT Director confirmed that Okta SSO is already provisioned in the AWS account and ready for integration, or does it require setup?
open_questions.impact_if_unanswered: If Okta is not provisioned, Phase 2 authentication development will be blocked. Fallback local authentication would add 1-2 weeks to Phase 3.

open_questions.question: What is the exact SAP API rate limit (requests per minute/hour) and the available batch window duration for nightly exports?
open_questions.impact_if_unanswered: If rate limits are more restrictive than assumed, the nightly export job will fail to complete within the window, causing data backlog and finance rework.

open_questions.question: Are there any additional SOC 2 control requirements beyond encryption at rest, audit logging, and access controls that must be implemented before go-live?
open_questions.impact_if_unanswered: If additional controls are discovered during Phase 3 security review, timeline will slip and budget may be exceeded.

open_questions.question: Who is the named post-launch owner responsible for maintaining the expense report tool after go-live (IT operations, finance team, or dedicated support)?
open_questions.impact_if_unanswered: If ownership is not assigned, the tool will become orphaned post-launch, leading to poor maintenance and user dissatisfaction.

deductions.reason: Assumption A1: QA allocation (0.5 FTE shared) is assumed protected but not explicitly confirmed in writing.
Assumption A2: PM allocation (0.5 FTE) is assumed sufficient for 3 stakeholders; lean but feasible.
Risk R2 (Integration): SAP API rate limits and batch window are assumed stable but not yet validated.
Risk R4 (Scope): Scope creep risk from stakeholders requesting additions during development.

pm_confidence_score.interpretation: PM confidence score is 82.0 because requirements are fully defined and signed off by CFO, team has direct experience with mandated stack, deadline is fixed and achievable with stated team, and all hard constraints are known. Deductions reflect two resource assumptions (QA and PM allocation) that are not explicitly confirmed in writing, plus integration and scope risks that are manageable with mitigation.
